title: Review of c23's CIPS inhibitor arrest: no division replicates (0 splits on fresh seeds 5, 6 and at dt/2), and the inhibitor cuts merges 3-4x, but the count is not flat on seed 6 (44 -> 37 bodies, mean area +22% from t=1500 to 3000, as fast as without inhibitor)
summary: Re-ran c23's world.py with the finding's inhibitor (DI 0.1, dI 0.01, kI 0.2, KI 0.5) and its kI=0 twin on fresh seeds 5 and 6 (128^2, t=3000), plus the inhibitor arm at the world's own dt halved (0.05, 600 frames) on seed 5. Persistent splits are 0 in all five runs. Without inhibitor: peaks 73/78 bodies, 28/31 merges, 58 -> 50 and 55 -> 47 bodies from t=1500 to 3000 (mean area +18%/+19%). With inhibitor: peaks 43/44, merges 7/9, 43 -> 41 on seed 5 (mean area +7%) but 44 -> 37 on seed 6 (+22%), where droplets keep coarsening by loss of small droplets rather than by merging (inh/seed6/sheet.png). The dt/2 run follows the dt=0.1 count series within one body at every sampled time, so the result is time-step converged. The negative (no division with a conserved enzyme) holds; the 'arrest at a fixed size' holds on 1 of 2 fresh seeds and is better described as fewer merges and a later, slower coarsening.

observations.finding: counts.txt: persistent splits 0 in 5/5 runs; merges 7/9 with inhibitor vs 28/31 without; t=1500 -> 3000 bodies 43 -> 41 (seed 5) and 44 -> 37 (seed 6) with inhibitor vs 58 -> 50 and 55 -> 47 without; inh/seed6/sheet.png: small droplets vanish between t=1560 and 3000 while large ones grow

seeds_run.result: partial: 0 splits, but count falls 44 -> 37 and mean area rises 22%, no arrest
dt/2 (world dt 0.05): same count series, 0 splits

controls_run.finding: noI/seed5, noI/seed6 (kI=0 twin, same seeds, grid, duration); inh_dt2 (world dt halved)

verdicts.limitation: Two fresh seeds at one parameter point and one grid (128^2); counts use threshold e > 0.5 and >= 6 px. c23 did not record the WORLD_P of its p_c arm in FACTS; I took the parameters from its summary. Longer runs would tell whether seed 5's plateau also gives way.
